title: Plan a 30-minute research talk on an ML-accelerated crystal structure prediction engine
hints: Write the one-sentence claim first, then cut every slide that does not support it. The 2-minute motivation is the claim plus why each half of the room should care, not the history of the field.
List the five questions you least want to be asked. For each, write the honest answer in two sentences and decide which one belongs on a limitations slide before anyone asks it.
rubric: The motivation takes at most 2 minutes and states the one question the talk answers in words both audiences can repeat, with the headline result given up front rather than saved for the end.

The talk is built around one key figure that shows the main claim against a baseline at equal compute with uncertainty, and the plan says what is said while it is on screen and how it is made legible for both audiences.
Every number in the plan is sourced (benchmark, baseline, DFT verification status) and a limitations slide names where the engine fails before the questions do.
The plan names one concrete thing each half of the audience can reuse (a method, a benchmark, a tool, a validation protocol) and what was deliberately cut to fit 30 minutes.
The plan prepares at least five hostile questions with two-sentence answers that concede what is true and point to data, and states a rule for handling a question the speaker cannot answer.
